name: The Beach Boys
hook: A family surf band whose leader stopped touring to make records, borrowed Phil Spector's method to do it, and pushed the Beatles to answer.
blurb: The Beach Boys formed in Hawthorne, California, in 1961: the brothers Brian, Dennis and Carl Wilson, their cousin Mike Love, and their friend Al Jardine. They were managed at first by the Wilsons' father, Murry, and signed to Capitol in 1962. Their early hits were about surfing and cars. One of them, 'Surfin' U.S.A.' (1963), set new words to Chuck Berry's 'Sweet Little Sixteen'. It was published by Berry's own publisher, Arc Music, from the start, and Berry's name was added to the credits from 1966. After a panic attack in December 1964, Brian stopped touring in January 1965 to stay in the studio. While the band toured, he made 'Pet Sounds' (May 1966) mostly with Phil Spector's session musicians, the Wrecking Crew. He has described it as his take on Spector's Wall of Sound, and said the Beatles' 'Rubber Soul' was what set him off. Paul McCartney said the Beatles took ideas from it for 'Sgt. Pepper'. 'Good Vibrations' (1966) was the most expensive single recorded up to then, and the 'Smile' album meant to follow it was shelved in 1967. Arguments about credit run through the band's history: Mike Love won a 1994 lawsuit for co-writing credit on many songs, including 'Surfin' U.S.A.'. Brian Wilson died on 11 June 2025, aged 82.
